items.lane: Lane A1 — SEO / Information Retrieval Science — PARTIAL INDEX
items.title: A1-1. GEO: Generative Engine Optimization — TARGET 1 ✔
items.text:
contents: Defines Generative Engine Optimization as a black-box framework for raising a source's visibility inside LLM-synthesized answers; introduces GEO-bench (10,000 queries, 25 domains) and 9 rewrite methods; citations/statistics/quotations additions gave up to ~40% visibility gain on its GPT-3.5 harness, ~22% on live Perplexity.
transfer: The founding measurement for GSE's AI-search play: galaxysportsedge.com pages should carry citeable statistics, quotations, and sourced claims in extractable form — the exact levers this paper measures — and GEO-bench's visibility metrics (position-adjusted word count, impression) are the template for a GSE citation-tracking eval in the research arm.

items.lane: Lane A1 — SEO / Information Retrieval Science — PARTIAL INDEX
items.title: A1-2. BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models — TARGET 6 ✔
items.text:
contents: Zero-shot IR benchmark of 18 datasets across 9 task types; 10 retrieval architectures compared; headline result — BM25 is a stubbornly strong zero-shot baseline, re-ranking/late-interaction models average best at high compute cost, dense/sparse models are cheaper but inconsistent out-of-domain.
transfer: Gives the research arm a ready-made, honest eval harness design for any GSE internal search/retrieval over its own corpus (picks archive, research library): train/tune on one domain, report nDCG@10 zero-shot on held-out domains, and never claim a neural retriever beats BM25 without this style of test.

items.lane: Lane A1 — SEO / Information Retrieval Science — PARTIAL INDEX
items.title: A1-3. MS MARCO: A Human Generated MAchine Reading COmprehension Dataset — TARGET 7 (paper) ✔
items.text:
contents: 1,010,916 anonymized real Bing queries with human-generated answers (182,669 fully rewritten) over 8,841,823 passages from 3,563,535 web documents; defines answerability, well-formed answer generation, and passage-ranking tasks.
transfer: MS MARCO passage ranking is the standard training/eval set for the retriever+reranker stack that decides which web pages an answer engine reads — the research arm can fine-tune/evaluate a reranker on it before trusting any claim about why a GSE page was or wasn't picked up by an AI engine.

items.lane: Lane A1 — SEO / Information Retrieval Science — PARTIAL INDEX
items.title: A1-4. The Anatomy of a Large-Scale Hypertextual Web Search Engine — TARGET 5 ✔
items.text:
contents: The original Google paper: crawler/indexer/repository architecture over 24M+ pages, anchor-text indexing, and PageRank as an objective citation-importance measure used to prioritize keyword-search results.
transfer: Anchor text + link graph as ranking inputs is the historical root of GSE discoverability: how other sites describe GSE in anchor text still shapes both classic ranking and what retrievers surface to LLMs — a concrete, checkable off-page lever, and core curriculum for the research arm's IR shelf.

items.lane: Lane A1 — SEO / Information Retrieval Science — PARTIAL INDEX
items.title: A1-5. Generative Engine Optimization at Scale: Measuring Brand Visibility Across AI Search Engines — TARGET 8 (GEO citation behavior) ✔
items.text:
contents: Field-scale GEO measurement: 100K+ prompt responses across 100+ brands on ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity/Gemini (Mar–May 2026); studies what engines value when citing a brand, which sources they rely on, and how visibility falls with brand size (~30 points per size step down, per secondary coverage).
transfer: Directly sizes GSE's problem as a small brand: it quantifies the small-brand visibility penalty in AI answers and names the source types engines lean on — the prioritization evidence for earning third-party/earned-media citations instead of only optimizing GSE's own pages.

items.lane: Lane A1 — SEO / Information Retrieval Science — PARTIAL INDEX
items.title: A1-6. Structured Linked Data as a Memory Layer for Agent-Orchestrated Retrieval — TARGET 8 (schema.org structured-data effects) ✔
items.text:
contents: Controlled 3×2 experiment (2,443 evals, 4 domains; Vertex AI Vector Search + Google ADK): Schema.org JSON-LD alone gives only a modest gain (Δ +0.17, p_adj = 0.024), while enhanced entity pages (linked data + llms.txt-style agent instructions + breadcrumbs) give +29.6% accuracy in standard RAG and +29.8% in agentic RAG (p < 10⁻²¹, d ≈ 0.60).
transfer: The most decision-useful schema result on the shelf: for GSE, plain JSON-LD is a minor lever — the measured win is full entity pages with typed relationships (players, teams, games, picks as linked entities) that an agent can traverse, which maps straight onto GSE's projections/rankings surface and its research-arm knowledge graph.

items.lane: Lane A1 — SEO / Information Retrieval Science — PARTIAL INDEX
items.title: A1-7. Manifest-Assisted Retrieval in Artificial Intelligence Search: Evidence Gaps and a Security Evaluation Framework for llms.txt — TARGET 8 (llms.txt) ✔
items.text:
contents: Evidence audit (39 sources) + security framework for /llms.txt: no retained source isolates an incremental utility effect of llms.txt over ordinary retrieval; a 15-tool study saw zero automatic llms.txt requests in 45 trials; a log study found 97% of domains with the file got no recorded requests (May 2026); defines 5 threat paths (incl. indirect prompt injection via manifest content) with a 120-response pilot.
transfer: Keeps GSE honest on llms.txt: ship one because it is cheap, but budget zero expected citation lift from it until a consumer demonstrably fetches it — and treat any third-party llms.txt/manifest content the GSE research arm ingests as an injection surface, per this paper's threat model.

items.lane: Lane A2 — Agent Discoverability + Web-Scale Datasets — Partial Index
items.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Specification — Architecture (revision 2025-06-18)
items.text:
contents: Client-host-server architecture on JSON-RPC, host/client/server roles, design principles, capability negotiation; remaining spec sections listed by name.
transfer: This is the exact interface for exposing GSE as an MCP server — publish GSE projections/rankings as MCP resources/tools with declared capabilities so any MCP host/agent can discover and call them instead of scraping the site.

items.lane: Lane A2 — Agent Discoverability + Web-Scale Datasets — Partial Index
items.title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification
items.text:
contents: Agent discovery via Agent Cards, capability negotiation, task management, JSON-RPC/gRPC/HTTP+JSON bindings, security — agents collaborate without exposing internal state.
transfer: A GSE Agent Card at a well-known URL is how other agents find and delegate to Galaxy Sports Edge — implement the card + a task endpoint and GSE becomes recommendable/delegable in agent ecosystems, not just searchable by humans.

items.lane: Lane A2 — Agent Discoverability + Web-Scale Datasets — Partial Index
items.title: A Survey of Agent Interoperability Protocols: MCP, ACP, A2A, and ANP
items.text:
contents: First systematic comparison of the four interoperability protocols — MCP for tools, ACP for messaging/discovery, A2A for delegation via Agent Cards, ANP for decentralized discovery with W3C DIDs/JSON-LD — plus a phased adoption roadmap.
transfer: The adoption roadmap is a direct build order for GSE: MCP server first, A2A card second, ANP/DID identity last — so the research arm can sequence discoverability work instead of guessing.

items.lane: Lane A2 — Agent Discoverability + Web-Scale Datasets — Partial Index
items.title: Evolution of AI Agent Registry Solutions: Centralized, Enterprise, and Distributed Approaches
items.text:
contents: Compares five agent-discovery registries — MCP Registry, A2A Agent Cards, AGNTCY Directory (IPFS/DHT), Microsoft Entra Agent ID, NANDA Index AgentFacts — on security, authentication, scalability, maintainability; this is the agent discovery / reputation-trust item for this lane.
transfer: Tells GSE exactly where to register to be found — MCP Registry listing + a self-hosted A2A Agent Card cover both the centralized and decentralized discovery paths, with verifiable identity as the trust signal agents will rank on.

items.lane: Lane A2 — Agent Discoverability + Web-Scale Datasets — Partial Index
items.title: ClueWeb22: 10 Billion Web Documents with Visual and Semantic Information
items.text:
contents: Construction of the 10B-page ClueWeb22 corpus (B/A/L subsets, HTML/text/link-graph/visual/semantic formats) sampled from the Bing index.
transfer: ClueWeb22's link-graph + page-importance sampling is the model for measuring how visible galaxysportsedge.com is in web-scale corpora — and its B subset is a ready training/eval corpus for the research arm's ranking work.

items.lane: Lane A2 — Agent Discoverability + Web-Scale Datasets — Partial Index
items.title: MS MARCO: A Human Generated MAchine Reading COmprehension Dataset
items.text:
contents: The MS MARCO dataset paper — 1,010,916 anonymized Bing queries, human answers, and the 8,841,823-passage collection that defines the passage-ranking task.
transfer: MS MARCO's query→passage relevance labels are the standard training signal for a reranker — the same reranking shape GSE needs so its own pages/projections surface first when agents and search engines retrieve sports answers.

items.lane: Lane A2 — Agent Discoverability + Web-Scale Datasets — Partial Index
items.title: Common Crawl URL Index (formerly Columnar Index) — Official Documentation
items.text:
contents: Parquet columnar index to the WARC corpus, full Athena table schema, and the real access path `s3://commoncrawl/cc-index/table/cc-main/warc/` (us-east-1, ~300 GB per monthly crawl, ~$1.50 max Athena scan as of Sep 2025); CDXJ index at index.commoncrawl.org.
transfer: One Athena query against this index answers "how many of our pages, from which crawls, with what fetch status" — a free audit of whether GSE is actually in the corpus that LLM/search builders train and retrieve from.

items.lane: Lane A2 — Agent Discoverability + Web-Scale Datasets — Partial Index
items.title: Common Crawl Host- and Domain-Level Web Graphs — Aug/Sep/Oct 2026 Release
items.text:
contents: Host graph 242.8M nodes / 2.4B edges; domain graph 135.0M nodes / 1.8B edges; BVGraph + text formats with published PageRank/harmonic-centrality ranks; access `s3://commoncrawl/projects/hyperlinkgraph/cc-main-2026-aug-sep-oct/host/` and `/domain/` (HTTPS prefix data.commoncrawl.org).
transfer: The published ranks file gives galaxysportsedge.com's actual host/domain centrality in the open web graph — a measurable baseline for link-building and for checking whether other sports sites out-rank GSE in the data agents are built on.

items.title: Dataset Cards — ClueWeb22 + MS MARCO Passage Ranking (card facts only)
items.text:

MS MARCO passage ranking — 8,841,823 passages, ~503K–532K labeled training queries, 6,980 dev queries, MRR@10, non-commercial research terms, direct TSV download from the official site/repo.

items.title: Model Context Protocol — Architecture, raw official markdown (2025-06-18)

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: A3-1 — Target 1: Fogg Behavior Model
items.url: https://archive.org/download/wikipedia-scholarly-sources-corpus/10.1145%252F100216.100217.zip/10.1145%252F1541948.1541999.pdf (Archive.org scholarly-sources corpus copy of the ACM paper, DOI 10.1145/1541948.1541999; the current behaviormodel.org homepage no longer links the PDF — see Gaps note).
items.text:
contents: Behavior = Motivation × Ability × Trigger, all three converging at the same moment; motivator pairs (pleasure/pain, hope/fear, social acceptance/rejection), six simplicity factors under Ability, and trigger types — the design grammar for any page that asks for an action.
transfer: Audit every GSE package page against B=MAT: motivation is highest right after a winning pick / big game (trigger timing), Ability is checkout friction (clicks, form fields, payment steps), and the Trigger must fire at that peak moment — a subscribe prompt buried on a generic page wastes the one moment all three factors align.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: A3-2 — Target 2a: Fogg credibility research (large study)
items.text:
contents: 2,684 people evaluated live websites; "design look" was the most-mentioned credibility factor (46.1% of comments), ahead of information structure and information focus — people judge credibility from surface design first, not from stated credentials.
transfer: For a paywalled picks site asking strangers for money, visual design IS the credibility argument: layout, typography, and consistency on the package pages will be read as proof of competence before any record or methodology is — design polish is not decoration, it is the first trust test the site either passes or fails.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: A3-3 — Target 2b: Fogg credibility research (theory)
items.text:
contents: Credibility impact = Prominence × Interpretation: an element only affects trust if it is (1) noticed and (2) judged favorably; prominence is driven most by user involvement, then topic, task, and experience.
transfer: A trust element nobody notices does nothing — GSE's record, sourcing, and honesty signals must be placed where a motivated visitor actually looks on the package page (near price and subscribe button), not parked on an About page; and each noticed element must be interpretable in one glance or it scores zero.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: A3-4 — Target 3: Social proof / online reviews meta-analysis
items.url: https://pure.rug.nl/ws/files/81643765/The_effect_of_electronic_word_of_mouth_on_sales_a_meta.pdf (University of Groningen research repository, publisher's version of record).
items.text:
contents: Meta-analysis of 1,532 effect sizes across 96 studies, 40 platforms, 26 product categories: eWOM is positively correlated with sales (r ≈ .091) on average, volume of word-of-mouth moves sales more than valence, and effects are stronger when receivers can judge their similarity to senders (homophily).
transfer: On GSE's site, member-count and testimonial VOLUME beats a few glowing quotes, and testimonials convert best when the reader can see the reviewer is like them (same sport, same package tier, same bankroll level) — collect many short, identified-by-profile member results rather than three polished endorsements.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: A3-5 — Target 4: Scarcity meta-analysis
items.text:
contents: Meta-analysis of 416 effect sizes from 131 studies: scarcity cues raise purchase intentions, but the type must match the product — demand-based scarcity works best for utilitarian products, supply-based scarcity for experiences, time-based scarcity for high-involvement products.
transfer: GSE packages are high-involvement experiences, so the evidence-backed levers are time-based (enrollment closes before kickoff / price rises Monday) and supply-based (capped member slots) scarcity — not generic "only X left" demand claims, which this meta-analysis says are the weakest match for this product type and the easiest to read as fake.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: A3-6 — Target 5a: Referral rewards and receiver responses
items.url: https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/server/api/core/bitstreams/cc65e63e-06f9-4c8a-862c-8996b832e525/content (Imperial College London Spiral repository, author manuscript).
items.text:
contents: Paying only the referrer backfires with receivers: they infer an ulterior motive and respond worse, especially for unsolicited and weak-tie referrals; rewarding BOTH sides, or using symbolic rewards, eliminates the negative effect.
transfer: GSE's referral program must be two-sided by design — "give a free week, get a free week" — never a referrer-only commission a friend can discover later; a one-sided bounty makes every member's recommendation read as a sales pitch and taxes exactly the trust that makes referrals convert.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: A3-7 — Target 5b: Referral reward structure, field experiment
items.text:
contents: Randomized field experiment on 160,000+ users of a Chinese telecom operator: uncertain (lottery-style) rewards for the SENDER plus a certain reward for the RECIPIENT raised total referrals 20.9%; uncertainty on the recipient's side cut referrals 12.3%, via perceived unfairness on the receiving end.
transfer: Precise split for GSE referral design: keep the new member's reward fixed and guaranteed (e.g., locked first-month discount — certainty is what makes them act), and put any gamification on the referrer's side only (chance at a free month), where uncertainty helps instead of hurting.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: A3-8 — Target 6: Sponsorship/affiliate disclosure effects
items.text:
contents: Text-mining plus a randomized experiment: disclosing sponsorship raises suspicion of ulterior motives and lowers attitudes/purchase intention for POSITIVE reviews, but does not hurt (and can help) when the review is negative or mixed — disclosure damage depends on review valence and reviewer credibility.
transfer: For GSE affiliate and partner placements (sportsbook links, sponsor mentions), disclosure is legally required and this paper prices it: expect a conversion cost on straight promotional copy, offset by keeping disclosed content specific and mixed (real pros/cons, named limits) rather than uniformly glowing — uniform praise plus a disclosure label is the exact combination readers punish.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: A3-9 — Target 7: Charm / just-below pricing, preregistered experiments
items.text:
contents: Two preregistered, high-powered experiments (N=729) comparing round ($10.00), just-below ($9.99), and precise ($9.87) prices: precise prices produced the most favorable price image and the most underestimation in recall, followed by just-below, then round — a modern, replication-grade check on the classic $9-ending claim.
transfer: GSE package pricing should be tested, not assumed: the classic charm ending is not the strongest option in this evidence — a precise price (e.g., $47 rather than $49.99 or $50) can read as more honest and more favorable for a data product, which fits a brand selling analysis rather than hype; A/B the three endings on the package page.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: The Wisdom of Amateur Crowds: Evidence from an Online Community of Sports Tipsters
items.url: University of Reading CentAUR repository (accepted version, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) — https://centaur.reading.ac.uk/78439/1/OddsportalEJORrev4.pdf
items.text:
contents: Aggregated Oddsportal amateur tipster predictions contain information not in betting prices; a majority-predict strategy returned an average 1.317% over 68,339 events (paper's figure), and selecting tipsters by experience or past accuracy did not improve returns — the accuracy stems from the whole crowd, not a skilled subset.
transfer: Direct test for GSE's pick-promotion model — it argues against marketing a "star capper" record and for publishing aggregated/consensus pick signals with full-sample returns; any GSE tipster leaderboard should be evaluated on whether subset selection beats the whole-crowd baseline this paper sets.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: The Wisdom of Large and Small Crowds: Evidence from Repeated Natural Experiments in Sports Betting
items.url: University of East Anglia UEA Digital Repository — https://ueaeprints.uea.ac.uk/id/eprint/67342/1/LargecrowdsIJoF_rev2.pdf
items.text:
contents: Using 13M+ Betfair prices (2008–2013, paper's figure), Queen's Club tennis prices became significantly less informative in years when a clashing soccer tournament reduced participation — larger prediction-market crowds forecast more accurately.
transfer: Participation-size evidence for GSE community/consensus products — forecast quality is a function of crowd size, so GSE should grow and retain its pick-community/pool participation (and disclose thin-participation windows) rather than treating a small follower count as an equally strong signal.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: The 'Wild West' of Wagering Affiliate Marketing and Implications for Gambling Harm
items.url: Author/journal OA version hosted as a static PDF copy of the Springer OA article — https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5ce7c889f96ff50001d4a103/t/68e210be0d5d824b02720874/1759645886993/A135+-+2025+-+Hing%2C+Rockloff%2C+Browne%2C+Russell%2C+Rawat%2C+Thorne%2C+Lole%2C+Sproston%2C+Hodge+-+The+Wild+West+of+wagering+affiliate+marketing+and+implications+for+gambling+harm+-+IJMHA.pdf
items.text:
contents: Exploratory Australian study, 44 key informants from 28 organisations; describes wagering affiliate payment/business models (incl. tipster/influencer affiliates) and identifies features informants said can increase gambling-harm risk, incl. incentives to target high-loss-potential bettors, and limited regulatory monitoring capacity.
transfer: The primary-source map of how wagering affiliate economics actually work — commission structures, targeting incentives, disclosure gaps — for GSE's affiliate lanes (OddsJam / Dabble / PrizePicks-class deals): which payment models create the documented harm/regulatory exposure, and which practices to contractually avoid before signing or promoting an affiliate offer.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: The High Cost of Direct Marketing from Wagering Operators, Tipsters and Affiliates: An Ecological Momentary Assessment of How Wagering Promotions Drive Betting, Expenditure, and Harm
items.url: REAL — Repository of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, hosting the OA journal article — https://real.mtak.hu/229793/1/2006-article-p1355.pdf
items.text:
contents: Ecological momentary assessment, 4,020 observations from 814 Australian at-least-fortnightly bettors over two weeks (paper's figures); users received on average 12.7 operator, 11.8 free-service and 21.7 tipster messages in two weeks (paper's figures), and bets, expenditure and short-term harm increased with each additional operator message, with digital-channel messages from free services/tipsters also associated with increased consumption and harm.
transfer: Dose-response evidence on promotional message frequency — directly usable to set GSE's own promo cadence caps for picks/plays/props pushes (email/text/app) and to document, for affiliate partners, that tipster-message volume itself is the measured exposure variable regulators are now studying.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: Effects of Inducements on Sports Gambling and Decision-Errors: An Experimental Study
items.url: Gambling Regulatory Authority of Ireland (GRAI) official CMS host — https://grai-cms-production-bucket.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/cms-media/2006-article-p959.pdf (same OA article also at REAL, https://real.mtak.hu/222988/1/2006-article-p959.pdf, HTTP 200 verified)
items.text:
contents: Preregistered randomised online experiment, 622 males under 40 betting on Euro 2024 matches (paper's figures); inducements increased amount spent by over 10%, almost halved the number opting not to bet, and made bettors three times more likely to choose a dominated "bad bet" (all paper's figures).
transfer: Causal (not correlational) effect sizes for free-bet / money-back style inducements — the benchmark GSE should use when evaluating sportsbook promo offers it promotes and when writing its own bonus-offer copy, including the documented decision-error effect that promo framing must not exploit.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: The Impact of Gambling Advertising Online: A Longitudinal Study on Exposure and Harm
items.text:
contents: Longitudinal representative Finnish adult survey, seven waves 2021–2024 (T1 N = 1,530; paper's figures); encountering gambling adverts online was directly linked to problem gambling, amplified problem gambling among online gamblers, and increased likelihood of debt enforcement, with unregulated offshore sites posing higher risk (paper's findings).
transfer: Longitudinal exposure evidence for GSE's online ad/promotion planning — separates onshore/regulated from offshore exposure risk, giving the research arm a citable basis for keeping GSE promotion inside regulated channels and for measuring exposure, not just clicks, in campaign reporting.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: Comparing Two Methods for Testing the Efficiency of Sports Betting Markets
items.url: Munich Personal RePEc Archive (University Library of Munich) — https://mpra.ub.uni-muenchen.de/121382/1/MPRA_paper_121382.pdf
items.text:
contents: Compares normalised-probability vs inverse-odds regressions for testing strong market efficiency; the normalised-probability method tests correctly while the inverse-odds method is biased against finding favourite-longshot bias, illustrated on large tennis and soccer datasets plus simulations (paper's design/claims).
transfer: Method paper for the GSE research arm's own efficiency/CLV testing — specifies which regression to use when GSE tests whether its picks/props prices show favourite-longshot bias, and warns that the common inverse-odds test will under-detect it; engine-training relevance: the normalised-probability construction is a directly implementable feature/label method for odds data.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: "Rich-Get-Richer"? Platform Attention and Earnings Inequality Using Patreon Earnings Data
items.text:
contents: Monthly Patreon earnings for n = 104,719 creators across 2018, 2021 and 2024 (paper's figures), segmented by single-platform affiliation (Instagram, Twitch, YouTube, Twitter/X, Facebook, Patreon-only); earnings tails fit a Pareto exponent α ≈ 2 (paper's figure), α declined/converged over time on most platforms, and more concentrated platforms had lower mean/median earnings.
transfer: The empirical distribution GSE's paywall pricing should be planned against — paid-creator earnings are power-law, not normal: median-creator revenue expectations, tier pricing, and conversion assumptions for GSE's paid pick packages should be modelled on this paper's per-platform percentiles, and its single-platform segmentation is a template for measuring whether X-driven vs YouTube-driven GSE subscribers convert differently.

items.lane: Lane A3 — Self-Selling Website Science (Persuasion, Conversion, Referral/Affiliate Mechanics)
items.title: goker/comp-serp-data — Comprehensive SERP Data (Target 5: promotion / discoverability)
items.text: transfer: A ready labelled SERP training set for GSE discoverability work — position/rank-tier as the label, content + Lighthouse features as inputs — to model which page features predict top-5 ranking for picks/props content pages, and as a feature schema for GSE's own SERP tracking of galaxysportsedge.com and affiliate landing pages.

items.lane: Lane B — Deep Books & Cross-Science Full Texts, Round 2 (2026-11-05)
items.title: 1. Statistical Physics — David Tong (Cambridge Part II lecture notes)
items.filename: `Tong-StatisticalPhysics-LectureNotes.pdf` — **191 pages**, verified first page ("Statistical Physics, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos, David Tong, DAMTP").
items.text:
contents: Microcanonical/canonical/grand canonical ensembles, classical and quantum gases, classical thermodynamics, phase transitions (Ising model, mean field, Landau theory, Lee–Yang zeros).
transfer: Ensemble/partition-function machinery is the same math underneath the engine's probability aggregation — phase-transition and critical-phenomena framing is a candidate lens for regime shifts in team performance (sudden collapses/streaks as near-critical behavior), and the Ising/mean-field treatment is a template for modeling interacting binary units (drives, possessions) with coupling terms.

items.lane: Lane B — Deep Books & Cross-Science Full Texts, Round 2 (2026-11-05)
items.title: 2. Kinetic Theory — David Tong (Cambridge graduate course, Michaelmas 2012)
items.text:
contents: Collisions and transport, BBGKY hierarchy, Boltzmann equation, H-theorem, stochastic processes (Langevin/Fokker–Planck), linear response and fluctuation–dissipation.
transfer: The stochastic-processes chapter is a full open textbook treatment of exactly the processes the engine's simulation layer uses; the Boltzmann-equation derivation (microscopic collisions → macroscopic distributions) is the physics template for going from play-level events to game-level outcome distributions without hand-waving.

items.lane: Lane B — Deep Books & Cross-Science Full Texts, Round 2 (2026-11-05)
items.title: 3. Fluid Mechanics — David Tong (Cambridge undergraduate course)
items.text:
contents: Euler and Navier–Stokes equations, basic flows, waves, hydrodynamic stability, turbulence introduction.
transfer: Stability analysis (when a small perturbation grows vs. damps out) maps directly onto in-game momentum questions — whether an early score differential is a stable state or a perturbation that mean-reverts; the wave/stability formalism gives the research arm a rigorous vocabulary for that question instead of narrative "momentum."

items.lane: Lane B — Deep Books & Cross-Science Full Texts, Round 2 (2026-11-05)
items.title: 4. Modeling the Cell Cycle: Why Do Certain Circuits Oscillate? — James E. Ferrell Jr., Tony Yu-Chen Tsai, Qiong Yang (Cell, 2011)
items.filename: `FerrellTsaiYang-2011-ModelingTheCellCycle.pdf` — **12 pages**, verified (title metadata + first page match).
items.url: Duke University course posting of the full text, https://courses.cs.duke.edu/cps262/current/pdf/ferrell.2011.pdf
items.text:
contents: ODE/Boolean/delay models of the CDK1/APC oscillator; what circuit topologies (negative feedback, coupled positive+negative feedback) produce oscillations; linear stability analysis.
transfer: The core lesson — oscillation requires negative feedback with delay plus nonlinearity, and coupled positive feedback makes it robust — is a design rule for any engine component that should cycle rather than saturate (e.g., fatigue/recovery state variables in player workload models, or market overreaction/correction cycles).

items.lane: Lane B — Deep Books & Cross-Science Full Texts, Round 2 (2026-11-05)
items.title: 5. Models in Biology: Lessons from Modeling Regulation of the Eukaryotic Cell Cycle — John J. Tyson & Béla Novák (BMC Biology, 2015, CC BY)
items.url: Publisher open access via BioMed Central, https://bmcbiol.biomedcentral.com/counter/pdf/10.1186/s12915-015-0158-9.pdf (also PMC4486427).
items.text:
contents: Thirty years of cell-cycle modeling distilled into model-building principles: start parsimonious, add mechanism only when data force it, hysteresis/bistability as explanations for irreversible transitions, parameter sloppiness.
transfer: Directly usable modeling discipline for the research arm: bistability/hysteresis explains one-way transitions (a team that has "lost the locker room" doesn't recover along the same path), and the parsimony-first rule is a check on the engine's tendency to add parameters faster than data can constrain them.

items.lane: Lane B — Deep Books & Cross-Science Full Texts, Round 2 (2026-11-05)
items.title: 6. Modelling the HRV Response to Training Loads in Elite Rugby Sevens Players — Sean Williams, Stephen West, Dan Howells, Simon P.T. Kemp, Andrew A. Flatt, Keith Stokes (J. Sports Science & Medicine, 2018, 17:402–408)
items.url: Europe PMC open-access render of PMC6090397 (journal OA).
items.text:
contents: Fits the Banister two-component impulse-response (fitness–fatigue) model to daily training loads and predicts chronic HRV (Ln rMSSD) out-of-sample; internal load (sRPE) markedly outperforms external load (high-speed distance) as the model input — 7 of 8 athletes met validity criteria with sRPE vs 1 of 8 with HSD.
transfer: Extends the shelved Banister material from performance outcomes to a *recovery biomarker* with a validation design the engine can copy: fit on 4 weeks, validate on the next 4, per-athlete. The input-selection result (subjective internal load beats GPS external load for predicting physiology) is a concrete warning for any workload feature built purely on tracking data.

items.lane: Lane B — Deep Books & Cross-Science Full Texts, Round 2 (2026-11-05)
items.title: 7. The Framing of Decisions and the Psychology of Choice — Amos Tversky & Daniel Kahneman (Science, 1981, 211:453–458)
items.filename: `TverskyKahneman-1981-FramingOfDecisions.pdf` — **7 pages** (journal scan incl. front matter), verified first page.
items.text:
contents: The Asian-disease problems and the framing-of-acts/contingencies/outcomes experiments; preference reversals from pure re-description; the decision frame defined.
transfer: Completes the shelved Kahneman–Tversky pair (1974 heuristics paper + 1979 Prospect Theory). For GSE content: how a pick is framed (win-rate vs. expected value vs. "avoid the loss") predictably changes audience response — framing is a measurable variable in content A/B tests, not a copywriting instinct.

contents: Individual heartbeat segments with arrhythmia class labels — a labeled physiological time-series classification set.
transfer: A clean, fully labeled signal-classification benchmark for the research arm's sequence models — the same train/validate discipline (beat-level labels, class imbalance, patient leakage risk between splits) that applies to play-by-play sequence classification in the engine.

items.url: https://zenodo.org/records/15006667 — "Machine Learning for predicting chaotic systems – Data" (the DeebDb/dysts benchmark distribution built on Gilpin's dysts library).
items.text:
contents: Noise-free test trajectories and forecasting/estimation tasks for dozens of named chaotic ODE systems.
transfer: A ready-made out-of-sample forecasting benchmark with known ground truth: any forecasting method the research arm wants to trust on sports time series can first prove itself here, where the data-generating process is known exactly and failure is measurable — the control experiment sports data can never provide.

items.lane: Lane C — Patents Round 2 + Hard Datasets (SEO, funnels, sports, science)
items.title: 1. Stanford University — US 6,285,999 B1 (2001) — 12 pp
items.text: transfer: The original authority-from-graph-structure algorithm. Directly reusable thinking for GSE: any internal corpus (papers, repos, accounts) can be ranked by citation/link endorsement rather than by self-description — the anti-guru filter in computable form. Also the math ancestor of the engine's network-centrality work already in the library (Barabási).

items.lane: Lane C — Patents Round 2 + Hard Datasets (SEO, funnels, sports, science)
items.title: 2. Google Inc. — US 8,938,463 B1 (2015) — 24 pp
items.text: transfer: The bias-correction pattern is the transferable asset: any GSE surface that learns from clicks (site search, content ordering, pick-page engagement) inherits position bias unless the selection model is debiased exactly this way. Same math applies to grading which content "performed" — raw CTR on position 1 is not evidence of quality.

items.lane: Lane C — Patents Round 2 + Hard Datasets (SEO, funnels, sports, science)
items.title: 3. Microsoft Corporation — US 7,664,735 B2 (2010) — 14 pp
items.text: transfer: A concrete, implementable recipe for diversifying any ranked output GSE ships — content feeds, recommended reads, package lineups — where ten near-identical items in the top slots destroy the funnel. Affinity-matrix re-ranking is computable from embeddings the stack already produces.

items.lane: Lane C — Patents Round 2 + Hard Datasets (SEO, funnels, sports, science)
items.title: 4. Google Inc. — US 8,572,075 B1 (2013) — 21 pp
items.text: transfer: This is an A/B discipline for ranking changes, written by the team that ran Google search quality: never ship a scoring change you cannot first diff against the incumbent offline. Maps one-to-one onto GSE's verdict-gate practice for engine changes — candidate vs incumbent, diff measured, ship decision second.

items.lane: Lane C — Patents Round 2 + Hard Datasets (SEO, funnels, sports, science)
items.title: 5. Amazon.com, Inc. — US 6,266,649 B1 (2001) — 22 pp
items.text: transfer: The cheapest recommender architecture that actually works at scale: precompute similarity once, serve lookups forever. For GSE content and package surfaces ("readers of this slate also took…"), item-to-item CF over content/packages needs no user model and no cold-start machinery — directly buildable from existing interaction data.

items.lane: Lane C — Patents Round 2 + Hard Datasets (SEO, funnels, sports, science)
items.title: 6. Amazon.com, Inc. — US 6,029,141 (2000) — 28 pp
items.text: transfer: The canonical affiliate-tracking design, in claims form: identifier in the link, credit at purchase, transparent reporting. This is the exact mechanism GSE's live affiliate accounts (Amazon Associates tag `galaxysportse-20`, OddsJam, Impact) implement from the other side — reading the merchant-side claims shows precisely which events are creditable and where attribution can silently break (identifier dropped mid-session = lost commission).

items.lane: Lane C — Patents Round 2 + Hard Datasets (SEO, funnels, sports, science)
items.title: 7. Intellions, Inc. — US 7,330,839 B2 (2008) — 13 pp
items.text: transfer: Pricing by experiment, not by opinion — the governed way to test GSE's package prices ($29–$49 today) instead of guessing: small sampled price cells, measured conversion, pick the optimum. Note the claims' discipline: sample size and duration are set *before* the experiment runs, which is the part most informal price tests skip.

items.text: transfer: This is the incumbent tracking-data prediction architecture (Lucey's group) written as claims: a baseline probability refined by spatial context features. It is the benchmark shape for any GSE tracking-derived feature work — and a freedom-to-operate read: the two-stage "initial probability → spatial feature refinement" pattern is claimed, so GSE's implementations should document their own differing construction.
